Jewish Cemetery of Bologna

Cemetery · Bologna, Italy

Bologna’s current Jewish cemetery is a sector within the Certosa municipal cemetery. The oldest section was opened in 1867 thanks to the efforts of Rabbi Marco Momigliano, who led the community from 1866 to 1896. A funeral chapel and numerous funeral monuments of artistic value made the cemetery the mirror of a community which had resettled definitively, after more than two centuries of exile. In 2010, following a thorough renovation project of the Jewish part of the cemetery, the Community decided to give greater visibility to the separate entrance on Via della Certosa. Guided visits are available, and advance reservation is recommended.
